mathgap.title: Signed Equality for Difference Statements
mathgap.principle: Interpret statements that equate two differences as signed equations preserving the order of names on each side: (A - B) = (C - D). Do not take absolute values.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says "the number of items that X has more than Y is equal to the difference between the number of items that P and Q have" or any similar equality of differences.
mathgap.example: Treating the equation as |X - Y| = |P - Q| (absolute values) leads to incorrect solutions.

mathgap.title: Iterative Substitution and Propagation
mathgap.principle: Whenever a variable's value becomes known, substitute it into all pending equations and simplify, propagating the information iteratively until no further substitutions are possible.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After each direct count or derived equation that fixes a variable's value.
mathgap.example: Leaving a known variable unchanged in later equations, preventing further simplification.

mathgap.title: Chronological Evaluation of Comparative Statements
mathgap.principle: Interpret comparative and difference statements using the counts as they exist at that point in the text; earlier statements affect later ones.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When processing statements sequentially, especially when a later statement references a person whose count was defined earlier.
mathgap.example: Using a person's initial count for a later comparison after a transfer has changed their count.

mathgap.title: Query‑Focused Subsystem Extraction
mathgap.principle: Identify the minimal subset of equations that involve the queried person directly or indirectly, and solve only that subsystem, ignoring unrelated statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When the problem contains many statements, most of which are irrelevant to the query.
mathgap.example: Attempting to solve the entire system of equations when only a few involve the queried person, leading to unnecessary work.

mathgap.title: Distinct Name Disambiguation
mathgap.principle: Treat each unique name as a separate variable, even if names differ by only a single character; avoid conflating them.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever the problem includes multiple similar‑sounding names.
mathgap.example: Confusing "Larry" with "Lara" and using the same variable for both.

mathgap.title: Preserve Order in "Difference Between" Phrases
mathgap.principle: When a phrase says "the difference between the number of items that A and B have", interpret it as the signed difference A - B, preserving the order as given.
mathgap.example: Interpreting "difference between A and B" as |A - B| or as B - A, swapping the order.

mathgap.title: General Comparative Interpretation (more/fewer)
mathgap.principle: Interpret "A has K more than B" as A - B = K, and "A has K fewer than B" as A - B = -K, preserving sign.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a comparative statement with "more" or "fewer" appears.
mathgap.example: Swapping direction and writing B - A = K instead of A - B = K.

mathgap.title: Direct Count Handling with Overrides
mathgap.principle: When a statement says "X has N items", set X's count to N at that point, overriding any previous value for X.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a direct count appears, regardless of its position in the text.
mathgap.example: Treating a later "X has N" as an initial count and ignoring earlier overrides.

mathgap.title: Chronological Transfer Application
mathgap.principle: Apply each transfer statement in the order given, subtracting the specified amount from the giver and adding it to the receiver before evaluating any subsequent statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a "X gives N items to Y" statement appears; ensure later statements use the updated counts.
mathgap.example: Ignoring a transfer and using the giver's pre‑transfer count in a later comparison.

mathgap.description: Swapped direction in "has K more than" statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: Model confuses the order of subtraction, treating the phrase as B = A + K instead of A = B + K.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always translate "A has K more than B" to A - B = K; for "fewer" use A - B = -K.

mathgap.why_it_happens: Model assumes differences are non‑negative and drops the order of terms.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Preserve sign and order when interpreting difference equations.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the chronological order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: Model treats transfers as independent of sequence, not updating counts before later statements.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply each transfer in order, updating giver and receiver before processing subsequent statements.

mathgap.description: Treating "has N" as an initial count regardless of position
mathgap.why_it_happens: Model assumes all direct counts are initial conditions and never overrides earlier values.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When a direct count appears, set the variable to that value at that point, overriding any previous value.

mathgap.why_it_happens: Model confuses "times" with addition, treating a multiplicative increase as additive.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret "increases by N times" as multiplication: new = old * N.
